segments.src: When the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5%, the effects rarely stay in the bond market.
segments.tr: When the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5%, the effects rarely stay in the bond market.

segments.src: They show up in monthly mortgage payments, in the listings that sit unsold, and in the spreadsheets of homebuilders deciding whether to break ground.
segments.tr: They show up in monthly mortgage payments, in the listings that sit unsold, and in the spreadsheets of homebuilders deciding whether to break ground.

segments.src: With the yield hovering near levels not seen in roughly two decades, home loan rates are staying stubbornly elevated.
segments.tr: With the yield hovering near levels not seen in roughly two decades, home loan rates are staying stubbornly elevated.

segments.src: Here is how that is squeezing buyers, sellers and builders heading into the fall.
segments.tr: Here is how that is squeezing buyers, sellers and builders heading into the fall.

segments.src: ## Why the 10-year yield matters for mortgages
segments.tr: ## Why the 10-year yield matters for mortgages

segments.src: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate does not move in lockstep with the Federal Reserve's policy rate.
segments.tr: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate does not move in lockstep with the Federal Reserve's policy rate.

segments.src: It tends to track the 10-year Treasury yield instead.
segments.tr: It tends to track the 10-year Treasury yield instead.

segments.src: Investors who buy mortgage-backed securities compare the return on those bonds with the safe return on government debt.
segments.tr: Investors who buy mortgage-backed securities compare the return on those bonds with the safe return on government debt.

segments.src: Lenders then price home loans to deliver a return above that benchmark.
segments.tr: Lenders then price home loans to deliver a return above that benchmark.

segments.src: The gap between the two is called the mortgage spread.
segments.tr: The gap between the two is called the mortgage spread.

segments.src: In calmer periods it has historically averaged somewhere around 1.7 percentage points.
segments.tr: In calmer periods it has historically averaged somewhere around 1.7 percentage points.

segments.src: In recent years it has often been wider, because of interest-rate volatility and uncertainty about how quickly borrowers will refinance or move.
segments.tr: In recent years it has often been wider, because of interest-rate volatility and uncertainty about how quickly borrowers will refinance or move.

segments.src: A higher Treasury yield plus a wider spread means a higher mortgage rate, even if the central bank holds its policy rate steady.
segments.tr: A higher Treasury yield plus a wider spread means a higher mortgage rate, even if the central bank holds its policy rate steady.

segments.src: ## What is pushing yields up
segments.tr: ## What is pushing yields up

segments.src: Several forces tend to lift long-term yields at the same time:
segments.tr: Several forces tend to lift long-term yields at the same time:

segments.src: - **Heavy government borrowing.** Large federal deficits mean more Treasury debt for investors to absorb, which can push up the yield needed to attract buyers.
segments.tr: - **Heavy government borrowing.** Large federal deficits mean more Treasury debt for investors to absorb, which can push up the yield needed to attract buyers.

segments.src: - **Sticky inflation.** If price growth cools more slowly than expected, investors demand more compensation for holding long-term bonds.
segments.tr: - **Sticky inflation.** If price growth cools more slowly than expected, investors demand more compensation for holding long-term bonds.

segments.src: - **A "higher for longer" policy outlook.** When markets expect the Fed to keep rates elevated, longer-term yields adjust upward.
segments.tr: - **A "higher for longer" policy outlook.** When markets expect the Fed to keep rates elevated, longer-term yields adjust upward.

segments.src: - **A larger term premium.** Investors may ask for extra yield to cover the risk of holding long-dated debt amid economic and political uncertainty.
segments.tr: - **A larger term premium.** Investors may ask for extra yield to cover the risk of holding long-dated debt amid economic and political uncertainty.

segments.src: No single factor explains the move, and analysts disagree about how much weight each one deserves.
segments.tr: No single factor explains the move, and analysts disagree about how much weight each one deserves.

segments.src: ## The squeeze on buyers
segments.tr: ## The squeeze on buyers

segments.src: For buyers, the arithmetic is unforgiving.
segments.tr: For buyers, the arithmetic is unforgiving.

segments.src: Consider a $400,000 loan on a 30-year fixed mortgage, counting principal and interest only:
segments.tr: Consider a $400,000 loan on a 30-year fixed mortgage, counting principal and interest only:

segments.src: | Mortgage rate | Approx. monthly payment |
segments.tr: | Mortgage rate | Approx. monthly payment |

segments.src: Going from 3% to 7% adds close to $1,000 a month on the same loan.
segments.tr: Going from 3% to 7% adds close to $1,000 a month on the same loan.

segments.src: Taxes, insurance and maintenance come on top of that.
segments.tr: Taxes, insurance and maintenance come on top of that.

segments.src: Many households that qualified comfortably a few years ago now find the numbers don't work, or they shop for a smaller home, a different neighborhood or a longer commute.
segments.tr: Many households that qualified comfortably a few years ago now find the numbers don't work, or they shop for a smaller home, a different neighborhood or a longer commute.

segments.src: Common responses among buyers include:
segments.tr: Common responses among buyers include:

segments.src: - **Rethinking the budget.** Some buyers now plan around the monthly payment instead of the headline price.
segments.tr: - **Rethinking the budget.** Some buyers now plan around the monthly payment instead of the headline price.

segments.src: - **Larger down payments.** Putting more money down reduces the loan amount and the interest paid over time.
segments.tr: - **Larger down payments.** Putting more money down reduces the loan amount and the interest paid over time.

segments.src: - **Adjustable-rate mortgages.** These offer lower initial rates but carry the risk of higher payments later. Borrowers should read the terms carefully.
segments.tr: - **Adjustable-rate mortgages.** These offer lower initial rates but carry the risk of higher payments later. Borrowers should read the terms carefully.

segments.src: - **Waiting.** Some renters are staying put until rates ease, though waiting has its own costs if prices or rents keep rising.
segments.tr: - **Waiting.** Some renters are staying put until rates ease, though waiting has its own costs if prices or rents keep rising.

segments.src: ## The "lock-in effect" and sellers
segments.tr: ## The "lock-in effect" and sellers

segments.src: Rates also affect the people who already own homes.
segments.tr: Rates also affect the people who already own homes.

segments.src: Millions of owners hold mortgages with rates far below today's levels.
segments.tr: Millions of owners hold mortgages with rates far below today's levels.

segments.src: Selling and buying again would mean swapping a cheap loan for an expensive one, so many choose to stay where they are.
segments.tr: Selling and buying again would mean swapping a cheap loan for an expensive one, so many choose to stay where they are.

segments.src: This is often called the lock-in effect.
segments.tr: This is often called the lock-in effect.

segments.src: It keeps the supply of existing homes for sale unusually low.
segments.tr: It keeps the supply of existing homes for sale unusually low.

segments.src: The result is a split market:
segments.tr: The result is a split market:

segments.src: - **Fewer listings** support prices in many areas, even though demand is weak.
segments.tr: - **Fewer listings** support prices in many areas, even though demand is weak.

segments.src: - **Longer time on market** for homes that are priced too high, which pushes some sellers to cut prices or offer concessions.
segments.tr: - **Longer time on market** for homes that are priced too high, which pushes some sellers to cut prices or offer concessions.

segments.src: - **Seller-paid incentives**, such as rate buydowns or help with closing costs, have become more common as a way to bring monthly payments down for buyers.
segments.tr: - **Seller-paid incentives**, such as rate buydowns or help with closing costs, have become more common as a way to bring monthly payments down for buyers.

segments.src: Sellers who must move for work, family or financial reasons face the toughest trade-offs.
segments.tr: Sellers who must move for work, family or financial reasons face the toughest trade-offs.

segments.src: They may need to price realistically and be flexible on terms.
segments.tr: They may need to price realistically and be flexible on terms.

segments.src: ## Pressure on builders
segments.tr: ## Pressure on builders

segments.src: Homebuilders feel the squeeze from both sides.
segments.tr: Homebuilders feel the squeeze from both sides.

segments.src: Higher mortgage rates cool demand.
segments.tr: Higher mortgage rates cool demand.

segments.src: Meanwhile, builders face their own borrowing costs for land and construction loans, along with the price of labor and materials.
segments.tr: Meanwhile, builders face their own borrowing costs for land and construction loans, along with the price of labor and materials.

segments.src: Because existing-home inventory is so tight, new construction has taken a larger share of the sales that do happen.
segments.tr: Because existing-home inventory is so tight, new construction has taken a larger share of the sales that do happen.

segments.src: Many builders have responded by:
segments.tr: Many builders have responded by:

segments.src: - offering mortgage rate buydowns or closing-cost credits,
segments.tr: - offering mortgage rate buydowns or closing-cost credits,

segments.src: - building smaller, more affordable floor plans,
segments.tr: - building smaller, more affordable floor plans,

segments.src: - slowing land purchases and new starts when demand softens.
segments.tr: - slowing land purchases and new starts when demand softens.

segments.src: If high rates persist, slower construction could limit future supply and keep housing costs elevated over the longer term, a trade-off that housing economists continue to debate.
segments.tr: If high rates persist, slower construction could limit future supply and keep housing costs elevated over the longer term, a trade-off that housing economists continue to debate.

segments.src: ## What it means for the broader economy
segments.tr: ## What it means for the broader economy

segments.src: Housing touches a large share of economic activity, from construction jobs and furniture sales to moving services and banking.
segments.tr: Housing touches a large share of economic activity, from construction jobs and furniture sales to moving services and banking.

segments.src: When transactions slow, those sectors feel it.
segments.tr: When transactions slow, those sectors feel it.

segments.src: Higher yields also raise borrowing costs for businesses and the government itself, which is one reason policymakers watch long-term rates closely.
segments.tr: Higher yields also raise borrowing costs for businesses and the government itself, which is one reason policymakers watch long-term rates closely.

segments.src: At the same time, higher yields are not all bad news.
segments.tr: At the same time, higher yields are not all bad news.

segments.src: Savers can earn more on Treasury securities, certificates of deposit and high-yield savings accounts.
segments.tr: Savers can earn more on Treasury securities, certificates of deposit and high-yield savings accounts.

segments.src: Those returns help offset higher costs for some households, particularly retirees who rely on interest income.
segments.tr: Those returns help offset higher costs for some households, particularly retirees who rely on interest income.

segments.src: ## Practical steps to consider
segments.tr: ## Practical steps to consider

segments.src: Every situation is different, but these general ideas come up often in consumer guidance:
segments.tr: Every situation is different, but these general ideas come up often in consumer guidance:

segments.src: 1. **Check your credit.** A higher score can qualify you for a better rate. Review your credit reports for errors before applying.
segments.tr: 1. **Check your credit.** A higher score can qualify you for a better rate. Review your credit reports for errors before applying.

segments.src: 2. **Compare lenders.** Quotes can differ meaningfully. Ask for a Loan Estimate from several lenders and compare both rates and fees.
segments.tr: 2. **Compare lenders.** Quotes can differ meaningfully. Ask for a Loan Estimate from several lenders and compare both rates and fees.

segments.src: 3. **Understand the total cost.** Look at points, closing costs and insurance, not just the interest rate.
segments.tr: 3. **Understand the total cost.** Look at points, closing costs and insurance, not just the interest rate.

segments.src: 4. **Ask about refinancing later.** If you buy now and rates fall, you may be able to refinance, but there is no guarantee. Check for fees and make sure the savings justify the cost.
segments.tr: 4. **Ask about refinancing later.** If you buy now and rates fall, you may be able to refinance, but there is no guarantee. Check for fees and make sure the savings justify the cost.

segments.src: 5. **Keep a cushion.** Make sure you can afford the payment and still have emergency savings.
segments.tr: 5. **Keep a cushion.** Make sure you can afford the payment and still have emergency savings.

segments.src: 6. **Talk to a professional.** A housing counselor, mortgage officer or financial adviser can help you weigh your options. HUD-approved housing counselors offer free or low-cost guidance in the United States.
segments.tr: 6. **Talk to a professional.** A housing counselor, mortgage officer or financial adviser can help you weigh your options. HUD-approved housing counselors offer free or low-cost guidance in the United States.

segments.src: ## What to watch this fall
segments.tr: ## What to watch this fall

segments.src: - **Inflation reports.** Cooler readings could ease pressure on yields. Hotter ones could add to it.
segments.tr: - **Inflation reports.** Cooler readings could ease pressure on yields. Hotter ones could add to it.

segments.src: - **Federal Reserve meetings.** Statements about the future path of rates often move the bond market.
segments.tr: - **Federal Reserve meetings.** Statements about the future path of rates often move the bond market.

segments.src: - **Treasury auctions and deficit news.** Demand for government debt influences yields.
segments.tr: - **Treasury auctions and deficit news.** Demand for government debt influences yields.

segments.src: - **Existing-home sales and builder sentiment.** These show whether buyers are adapting or pulling back.
segments.tr: - **Existing-home sales and builder sentiment.** These show whether buyers are adapting or pulling back.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## The bottom line

segments.src: A 10-year Treasury yield above 5% is a reminder that mortgage rates are shaped by forces well beyond any one lender or homebuyer.
segments.tr: A 10-year Treasury yield above 5% is a reminder that mortgage rates are shaped by forces well beyond any one lender or homebuyer.

segments.src: For now, elevated yields are keeping borrowing costs high, holding many owners in place and testing builders' margins.
segments.tr: For now, elevated yields are keeping borrowing costs high, holding many owners in place and testing builders' margins.

segments.src: No one can say for sure when conditions will change, and forecasts have a mixed record.
segments.tr: No one can say for sure when conditions will change, and forecasts have a mixed record.

segments.src: The most useful approach for most households is to focus on what they can control: their budget, their credit and their time horizon.
segments.tr: The most useful approach for most households is to focus on what they can control: their budget, their credit and their time horizon.
